passages.title: The history of writing
passages.body:
The history of writing

The earliest form of writing was developed around 3300 BC by a group of people
called the Sumerians who lived in Ancient Mesopotamia. Until then, the
Sumerians had mostly lived by hunting, but around that time, they decided to
settle in the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, where the soil was [5]
perfect for growing crops. There they became some of the first farmers.

As their way of life developed, the Sumerians needed to remember detailed
information about what they were buying and selling and the work the
government was doing. So, to help them make permanent records, they
developed a system of symbols. This early writing was done on tablets of wet [10]
clay with a pointed stick called a stylus. Once the clay dried, the information
could be stored for later.

In the beginning, Sumerian writing consisted of simple pictures called
pictograms. But gradually, the system was extended to include sounds as well as
meanings. People who trained as writers were called scribes. They used the [15]
stylus to make wedge¹-shaped marks in the clay. This type of writing is called
cuneiform writing.

Understanding Mesopotamian writing is difficult. This is because there were over
700 symbols. The symbols often varied between cities and many of them
changed over time as well. Luckily, experts have deciphered many Sumerian [20]
tablets. This is how we have learned so much about Mesopotamian life,
government and history.

While most of the Sumerian tablets that have been discovered are government
and business records, some include poetry, songs, tales of heroes and myths
about Mesopotamian gods. [25]

About 300 years later, the Ancient Egyptians began to develop a writing system
known as hieroglyphics, which used thousands of picture words called
hieroglyphs. Some symbols represented entire words, but others represented
sounds, just like the letters in English.

One of the aims when writing hieroglyphs was to produce writing that looked [30]
beautiful. Since it was quite challenging to write hieroglyphs, becoming a scribe
took many years of education and practice, and children started training at six or
seven years of age. Being a scribe in Ancient Egypt was considered a good job
because they did not have to join the army or pay taxes. Only children from rich
families could train as scribes. [35]

The Ancient Egyptians often used clay tablets for writing but they also wrote on a
type of paper made from a tall, reed-like plant called papyrus. To make the
paper, they used two strips from the plant's stem and layered these in opposite
directions. Next, they covered the strips with a type of cloth called linen and
flattened them with a mallet. After a while the strips would stick together, creating [40]
a single sheet to write on.

For many years nobody knew what the Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs meant.
Then in 1799, a special stone, now known as the Rosetta Stone, was found in
Egypt. This was a very significant find because the same message was written
on it, in both Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs and in Greek. Archaeologists were [45]
able to read the Greek message on the stone and used this to translate the
hieroglyphs. They were then able to use this translation to work out the meaning
of other Ancient Egyptian texts.

Glossary

¹wedge: triangle

sections.title: Section A: Reading
sections.instructions: Spend 30 minutes on this section. Read the text in the insert, and answer Questions 1–13.

items.stem:
Look at the first paragraph (lines 2–6).

Give one word which means ‘mainly’.

Look at the first paragraph (lines 2–6).

Give one reason why the Sumerians chose to live in that part of Ancient Mesopotamia.

accepted: The land was good for growing crops
the soil was perfect for growing crops
the soil was good for growing crops
they didn't want to be hunters
they did not want to hunt any more

items.note: Mark scheme: any of — the land was good for growing crops / near the rivers; so they could become farmers / they didn't want to be hunters. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Which form of writing would you like to try doing yourself: Egyptian or Sumerian?

Write your choice, then explain it using two pieces of evidence from the text.

Evidence 1:
Evidence 2:

accepted: Sumerian: I would like to try making pictograms
Sumerian: I would like to try drawing pictograms
Sumerian: I would like to try writing pictograms
Sumerian: I would like to try cuneiform because it was the first form of writing
Sumerian: I would like to try making wedge shapes using a stylus on clay
Egyptian: I would like to try writing on papyrus paper
Egyptian: I would like to try writing hieroglyphs because they were beautiful

items.note: Mark scheme: 1 mark for each piece of evidence (max 2). If Sumerian: pictograms; cuneiform was the first form of writing; wedge shapes with a stylus on clay. If Egyptian: writing on papyrus paper; hieroglyphs were beautiful. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

Evidence 2:

items.stem:
Write an article for your school website about a very old place that you know about.

It could be:
• a place where something important happened in the past
• an old or famous building – a castle, a palace
• an ancient city or ruins
• a religious building
• your own idea.

Plan your article first, then write it.
